key_claims: Iron deficiency is common in endurance athletes because the recommended daily allowance is on the low side for this population
Heme iron (from animal products) is easier to absorb than non-heme iron, and vitamin C enhances absorption while tannins and caffeine inhibit it
B12 is not found naturally in non-fortified plant-based foods and is essential for oxygen-carrying capacity in endurance athletes
Vitamin D supplementation at 1000 IU daily is critical for cyclists due to low-impact training compromising bone density
Antioxidants like vitamin C should be periodized during training cycles to avoid dampening the free radical stress response needed for fitness adaptation
specific_numbers: Blood tests a couple of times a year
Once or twice a year crashes mentioned as inevitable for cyclists
cluster_reasoning: Episode focuses on supplementation strategy (iron, B12, vitamin D, omega-3, antioxidants) and their physiological effects on endurance performance, which is core nutrition content; recovery is secondary because vitamin D and antioxidant periodization touch on adaptation and bone health.
